title: kv cache: improve memory management and eviction (paging + spillover + fragmentation)
author: Ben Carter
description: Motivation: We see frequent OOMs and higher-than-expected fragmentation in the KV cache under mixed chat/streaming workloads. Large variance in per-request KV sizes combined with long-lived conversation prefixes causes inefficient packing which increases resident memory and forces evictions that hurt P99 latency. This PR implements a multi-pronged memory management and eviction strategy to reduce fragmentation, enable transparent paging to host memory, and provide a disk-backed spillover for cold KV shards. Design/changes: 1) size-aware LRU: evictions are now weighted by estimated serialized byte-size rather than entry count; this reduces churn when many small entries would otherwise evict a single large prefix. 2) slab-style allocator + compaction: shard-level allocator reduces internal fragmentation; a background compactor coalesces free ranges during low load windows. 3) paging + host spillover: large/least-recent shards can be asynchronously paged out to host RAM (mmap-backed pages) and, when host memory pressure is high, to a compressed disk spillover store (lz4), with lazy rehydration. 4) multi-tier eviction policy: hot (in-GPU), warm (host-paged), cold (disk-spill) tiers with automatic promotion on access. 5) memory accounting and backpressure: request admission now considers expected KV growth and can trigger prefetch/rehydration heuristics. 6) metrics + tracing: new metrics for fragmented_bytes, spill_count, page_out_rate, rehydrate_latency, per-shard_free_ranges, and per-request cache_pressure. 7) config knobs: per-tenant tiering thresholds, spill directory, compressor, compaction window, and resident_ratio targets. Benchmarks: synthetic mixed chat workload (50% chat, 30% embeddings, 20% streaming) with long conversations: 18% drop in P99 token latency under memory pressure, 35% fewer OOM/eviction events in steady-state, average GPU resident memory reduced by ~22% with comparable throughput. Implementation notes: - Introduces new module redwood/serving/kv_cache/allocator.rs and spillover.rs that implement allocator, compactor, pager, and disk store. - Adds runtime flags and dynamic config under redwood/config/cache.toml. - Adds end-to-end integration tests under redwood/serving/tests/kv_cache_paging.rs and unit tests for allocator behavior. - Backwards compatible: existing on-disk KV formats supported; fallbacks used when spillover disabled. Rollout plan: merge behind feature-flag enabled by default in staging. Canary rollout to Dedicated nodes for one week with increased metrics retention. Monitor fragmentation and rehydrate_latency, revert knob to previous policy if error budget consumed. Docs: includes new observability docs and runtime tuning guide in redwood-docs/observability/kv-cache.md. Related: addresses ENG-1523 and reduces tickets like SUP-987. Checklist: - [x] allocator and compaction implementation - [x] paging + spill store - [x] end-to-end and unit tests - [x] metrics and dashboards - [x] integration with admission/backpressure - [x] docs and release notes
commits: 5 commits: 1) allocator: initial slab allocator + APIs; 2) compactor: background compaction and tests; 3) pager: host paging and mmap-backed pages; 4) spillover: disk LZ4-backed cold store and serialization; 5) config+metrics+tests: hooks, dashboards, and integration tests.

release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: size-aware eviction, slab allocator and compaction, host paging, disk spillover; reduced OOMs and lower P99 under memory pressure. Config knobs for per-tenant tiering and spillover. See redwood/docs/observability/kv-cache.md for tuning.
